newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Islamic groups battle in south Russia, two killed.
newsitem.headline: Islamic groups battle in south Russia, two killed.

text.p: At least two people were killed and 10 were taken hostage in a gunbattle between rival Islamic groups in a village in Russia's southern Dagestan region, police said on Tuesday.
At least two more were seriously hurt and taken to hospital after about 1,000 people started fighting on Monday night in a North Causasus village near the breakaway region of Chechnya.
The conflict continued into Tuesday, prompting local police to send in reinforcements to restore order, said a spokeswoman for regional police in the Dagestan capital Makhachkala.
It was unclear what prompted the fighting.

The town's majority Moslem group took 10 adherents of the Wahabi sect hostage, police said. The official doctrine of the reigning house of Saudi Arabia, the Wahabi sect favours traditional Islamic values.
"The situation has worsened in the region. Unfortunately, it happens quite often in our republic," another police spokesperson said.

Dagestan, a region of some 30 different ethnic groups, has been troubled occasionally by violence spilling over from Chechnya, where Russian troops fought separatists for nearly 21 months until a truce was signed last August.

The fighting began just hours after Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov signed a peace accord on Monday, promising an end to 400 years of intermittent conflict between Moscow and independence-minded Chechnya.
